title: How Many Inactive Wells Remain? | CAPIT Data Context
description: Understanding inactive, orphaned, and idle well counts across state and federal inventories.
headline: How Many Inactive Wells Remain?
body: The scale of legacy oil and gas infrastructure in the United States is vast. Current estimates point to a highly fragmented landscape of over 3.5 million abandoned, idle, or orphan wells requiring attention. Understanding these figures requires careful navigation of varying state definitions, update schedules, and agency reporting standards.

sections.heading: Orphaned vs. Inactive Infrastructure
sections.body: To grasp the scale of the challenge, it is important to understand the regulatory distinctions:
bullets: **Orphaned Wells:** High-priority wells with no solvent operator legally responsible for their plugging and site restoration. These are the primary targets for state and federal remediation grants.

**Inactive / Idle Wells:** Wells that are not currently producing but may still have a solvent operator on record. These are tracked by state regulatory commissions and are subject to varying compliance deadlines.

sections.heading: The Necessity of Transparent Tracking
sections.body: Currently, information regarding these wells is deeply fragmented across individual state agencies, private sector efforts, and federal initiatives. A single state may expose only partial subsets of its inventory, making it exceedingly difficult to gauge the true national picture. Transparent tracking is essential to effectively target remediation efforts and measure national progress. CAPIT continuously normalizes data from disparate state and federal inventories into a single, cohesive public experience. By bringing this information out of fragmented databases and onto a transparent ledger, CAPIT helps the public, landowners, and policymakers understand exactly what is being counted, where it is located, and how much work remains to secure America's energy legacy.
